name: Companion
tagline: One small terracotta creature on a cool slate desk; everything else sits still.
mood: A cool, tidy desk with one tiny warm living thing on it: you read the work at a glance and check on the creature the way you check on a pet.
rationale: The owner's complaint is two complaints: no rhythm, and no character. Rhythm comes from a layout with almost nothing to align, a nook and two edges. The header is the creature's nook: its body on cells 2-5 and, after one cell of air, a nameplate whose three rows all start at cell 7; it is the only block on the page that starts past cell 2. Every row beneath it sits on two edges and nowhere else: the left edge at cell 2 (section labels, and status glyphs with their text at cell 4; steps are not nested under their phase, the phase is one more row) and the right edge flush on cell 71 (one fact per row: sha, agent, age, `blocks B4`, the chips, a signal's meta). There are no label columns, no rules, no padEnd and no middle column, so the same tree aligns in a proportional font, and one blank line before each section is the only vertical punctuation. Character is exactly one playful element: a 4x3-cell creature, a cousin of the one above the chat input (block body, dot eyes, terracotta), that blinks, looks down when a question waits, hops when the gate passes and droops while it is red. It sits directly above the left edge where every status glyph lives, so when it looks down its gaze lands on the `?` it is worried about. The desk under it is cool slate with no warm tint anywhere (the hover tint is slate, the eyes are the desk showing through the face, error stays the `error` key and the palette reads it as a rose red, so the health `!` never looks like part of the body one cell away), so the `claude` terracotta is the only warm mark on a cold desk and the eye finds the creature first, then the work. On the band and on surfaces without cells it is one `◉` mark in the same color.
tokenMap: bg/fg: the terminal's own background (never painted) and the `text` key. The slate in the palette is how the theme asks to be pictured; what it actually does in the pane is keep every neutral cool or hue-free: `text`, `inactive` and `subtle` are grey keys, accent2 and bg2 are slate, and no word is ever tinted, so `claude` is the only accent hue on screen. Painting the pane slate was rejected on purpose: a pane-sized hex background would fight the person's own terminal colors. dim: `dimColor` for meta and the past (right-edge facts, done steps, the branch, signal names); section labels are dim + bold. accent: the `claude` key everywhere it appears and nowhere else: the creature's body and eye cells in the Client (its surface draws with the ordinary Box/Text table, so theme keys work there and no hex is needed), the band's `◉` at >= 100 columns, and the static `◉` on VS Code and mobile; the palette pair only documents what `claude` resolves to in the default dark and light themes. accent2: the `inverseText` key (an engine ThemeKey beyond the brief's summary list; `<Text inverse>` on the eye cells is the equivalent without a second key), used for the two eye cells when the Client paints the face row's middle cells with a `claude` background (the filled face, the default), so the eyes read as the desk showing through the face; it is never used outside the Client, and the markup mock shows the outline form (eyes in `claude` on the terminal bg) because tags cannot set per-cell backgrounds. bg2: the hover background on keyed rows (needs rows, the phase row, step rows) and the Needs-you option buttons (Box `hover.backgroundColor`), the one hex the theme sets, slate in both modes (#20242a dark, #e6eaef light); the hooks module reads the `theme` row from `$.config.list()` at session start and again on every `config.set` event whose key is `theme` (so a /config switch mid-session re-picks it), picks the light value when the row's value starts with `light` (`light`, `light-daltonized`, `light-ansi`), the dark value otherwise (absent, Claude Code's default is dark), and passes the pick to the draw in the view data. The Button label inside a hovered row is additionally inverted by the engine itself. success/warning/error: the theme keys `success`/`warning`/`error`, unchanged in meaning (meter fill, done/doing and the gate's pass glyph; decisions and drift; blockers and a red gate). They are warm or cool by meaning, not by tint; the palette's sage, straw and rose only show a reading in which none of them sits in the terracotta's hue, which is what keeps the health `!` one cell from the face from reading as part of the creature. bold: `bold` for the current phase row `▶ B UI`, the `▶B` chip, the doing step and the active footer tab, so "current" is wayfinding on theme colors, not hex. The footer's hotkey color (`1:`) is the engine's own accent for plain Buttons, not set by the theme.

otherTabs: Every tab keeps the nook (creature on cells 2-5, nameplate from cell 7) and the footer, so the creature never jumps, and every tab keeps the two edges below it. Plan is a flat list on the left edge: each phase row is bold with its fold glyph (`▾`/`▸`) in the glyph cell, its key and title at cell 4 and its count on the right edge, with one blank line above it (the section rhythm, so phases read as groups without nesting); its steps follow at the same edge with the same right-edge facts (sha, agent, `? D1`), and a folded phase is the one row. Log: newest first, the entry's text at cell 4, the glyph cell holding `✓` (success) for a step done and empty otherwise, Rulings' text in warning, the time (`16:40`) as the right-edge fact. Step details: a nav row (`‹ B2   B4 ›`) under the nook, then fields on the two edges: dim name and short value on the left (`status doing`, `agent opus 6m · Edit`), the sha or time on the right, longer prose wrapping at cell 4. Needs you: each question is a block: `?` at cell 2, the question bold at cell 4, `blocks B4` on the right edge; beneath it at cell 4, dim `asked 16:05`, the `why` prose, and the options as `[ per seat ]` buttons with the recommended one primary, inverted by the engine under the pointer and tinted bg2 on hover; the creature looks down at the open question until it is answered, then blinks once and rests. Finished runs show `✓` health, `took 3h40m` on the nameplate's right edge, and the creature with its eyes up.
glyphs: Statuses are the kit set, unchanged, so nothing has to be relearned: todo `○` (dim) · doing `●` (success, bold) · done `✓` (success, row dim) · blocked `!` (error) · skipped `–` (dim) · current phase `▶` (bold) with chips `✓A  ▶B  ○C` · decision `?` (warning) · blocker `!` (error) · drift `~` (warning) · health `▶` working, `!` needs you, `✗` gate red, `✓` finished · meter `━` filled (success) and `─` empty (dim), 10 cells on the band, 20 in the nameplate. All of them live in one glyph cell, cell 2, the left edge; SIGNALS uses it for the gate's own state (`✓` passed in success, `●` running, `✗` red in error) and leaves it empty for git and ctx, and the name beside it is dim so `✓ gate` never scans as a done step. The creature is built from `▗ █ ▖ ▐ ▌ ▝ ▀ ▘ ▄` and braille eye cells: rest `⠘⠃`, closed `⠠⠄`, looking down `⠰⠆`, looking up `⠈⠁`. Where there is no room or no cell grid (the band at >= 100 columns, VS Code, mobile) the creature is one static `◉` in `claude`, the same sign everywhere. All width-1 BMP, no emoji.
spacingRules: A nook and two edges. Cell 1 is the left pad, cell 72 the right pad. The nook: the header is a row Box of the creature (cells 2-5), one cell of air, and a nameplate column whose three rows all start at cell 7: the health glyph at 7 and the title at 9; branch · gate command at 7; the meter at 7 with `7/18` hugging it after one space (count and meter are read together). It is the only block indented past cell 2, so the creature owns that gutter and nothing below enters it. The nameplate's right edge holds elapsed (row 1) and agents (row 2); row 3 has none. The two edges: below the nook every row has exactly two anchors. The left edge is cell 2: section labels (dim bold uppercase, no rule) and status glyphs, with the row's text at cell 4 after one space; a row with no state (git, ctx) leaves its glyph cell empty so its name still starts at cell 4. The right edge is cell 71, reached with a flexGrow spacer, never space padding, and holds one fact per row: `blocks B4`, an age, the phase count, a sha, an agent, `? D1`, PLAN's chips (two spaces between chips), a signal's meta. Nothing sits between the edges but the row's own text: no nesting (the phase row `▶ B UI` is one more row on the left edge, bold, its steps beneath it at the same edge), no label columns, no label Boxes, no padEnd, no middle column. A signal row reads glyph, dim name, value on the left (`✓ gate passed 4m ago`) and its meta on the right (`took 52s`), so the value stays next to its name and only the meta travels to the edge. Text clips with `…` at least two cells before the right-edge fact. Vertical: exactly one blank line above each section label and above the footer (`marginTop={1}`), none inside a section, none inside the nook. Band: segments joined by ` · `, counts pinned right with two spaces between them and at least four cells of air before them; when the bar drops, the count and the step keep the two-space join the code draws today. Footer at cell 2: the engine's `1: Name` chips with a gap of 3, the active name bold. Never adjacent: a glyph and its text (always one space), two right-edge facts on one row, a section label and the row above it, the creature and the health glyph (one cell of air).
desktopNotes: Desktop: the creature is the same Client (the desktop supports Client), drawing its 4x3 grid in the app's monospace code face; if the desktop Client region is not a cell grid, it falls back to the `◉` mark in the nook. Everything else is the identical tree: the nook is a row Box (creature, then the nameplate column), so the nameplate rows start together in a proportional font; below it every row is the same flex children (glyph, text, flexGrow spacer, fact), so the left edge, the text start and the right edge hold without any measured width. The theme has no `────` rules, no label Boxes and no space padding to break, so the current isMono split for section heads disappears. VS Code and mobile: no Client and no band; the nook holds one static `◉` in `claude` beside the nameplate (the same row Box, so the nameplate keeps its own left edge), a long title wraps inside its flex child while the fact stays on the right edge, options are buttons and the reply is "Reply in chat". On every surface the pane draws on the host's own background; the slate is the theme's picture, and bg2 is the hover tint on terminal and desktop.

animation.idea: One 4x3-cell creature in the nook reacts to the run: it blinks now and then when idle, looks down at the left edge (NEEDS YOU sits directly below it) while a question waits, does a squash-and-stretch hop when the gate passes, and sits down with its eyes closed while the gate is red. Frames (rows top to bottom): rest `▗██▖ / ▐⠘⠃▌ / ▝▀▀▘`; blink `▗██▖ / ▐⠠⠄▌ / ▝▀▀▘`; ask `▗██▖ / ▐⠰⠆▌ / ▝▀▀▘`; hop = squash `▗▄▄▖ / ▐⠘⠃▌ / ▝▀▀▘` then stretch `▗██▖ / ▐⠈⠁▌ / ▝▀▀▘` then rest; droop `(blank) / ▗▄▄▖ / ▐⠠⠄▌`; finished `▗██▖ / ▐⠈⠁▌ / ▝▀▀▘`. It is the only warm thing on the desk and the only thing that moves; the nameplate beside it, the ledger below and the band's `◉` (plain static Text) never animate.
animation.trigger: Mood follows state at once: a decision or blocker added -> ask pose; answered -> one blink, then rest; a gate run that passed and is newer than the last one the Client saw -> hop, once; D6 (gate red) -> droop until green; worklog status done -> finished pose. Blinks fire on a random 4-9 s interval while idle (every 10-15 s in droop); nothing else moves.
animation.cadence: One `surface.every(250)` timer for the instance's life (started once, while state is undefined, as the Client contract asks); each tick compares the due frame with the drawn one and calls setState only when it differs, so the region repaints a few times a second during a hop and otherwise once per blink. A blink is one 250 ms frame (closed, then open on the next tick); the hop is three frames at 250 ms (squash, stretch, rest). If the hooks module can observe prompt activity it passes `quiet: true` in props and blinks pause while the person is typing; without that signal the idle motion is at most one 250 ms blink every 4 s. Mood changes arrive through props on the next tree redraw (seconds), never per frame.
animation.staticFrame: The mood pose with the eyes open, which is what the mock shows: `▗██▖ / ▐⠰⠆▌ / ▝▀▀▘`, the 'question waits, looking down at the left edge' frame, since D1 is open in the sample and its `?` sits at cell 2 two rows below the face. With nothing waiting it is the rest frame `▗██▖ / ▐⠘⠃▌ / ▝▀▀▘`; with the gate red the droop frame. Each is good on its own, is what VS Code/mobile would show if they had cells, and the `◉` is its stand-in where there are none.

feasibility: Everything in the mock is Box/Text/Button on theme keys; no rules, no label Boxes, no Raster/Image/Svg, and the only mono-only drawing is the creature. The two edges are a removal more than an addition: stepRow loses its level indents, needsBlock its 2-cell indent, signalsBlock and stepDetail their padEnd, and each row becomes glyph, text, flexGrow spacer, fact. The nook is one row Box. The creature needs a Client (terminal and desktop only); its surface draws with the ordinary element table (ClientElements is the terminal table minus Client/Raster/Image), so `color="claude"` and `backgroundColor="claude"` work there and the theme sets no hex for it. Quarter blocks and braille render in every modern terminal font, but a font without the quadrant glyphs would show tofu, and the Client cannot detect that, so the fallback is a mod setting `companion: full | face | off` (default `full`; `face` draws the middle row `▐⠘⠃▌` alone beside the nameplate's middle row; `off` draws the `◉` mark). The band's `◉` is a Seg inside bandSegments (drop 0, only at columns >= 100) so it is counted by the drop loop and the title clip, and the band stays one row at any title length. The footer's hotkey rendering is the engine's own (`1: Overview`, hotkey in its accent); the label is the bare name and the active tab's label is a bold Text chip, which Button accepts. bg2 is the one hex, a slate pair selected by the `theme` row of `$.config.list()` (a declared /config row) and re-picked on `config.set` events for that key; if the read fails the dark value is used and the hovered label is still readable because the engine inverts it on its own. The cool desk costs nothing at runtime: it is the absence of warm tints, not a painted background. New behavior, listed under implementation: two right-edge facts on step rows (`? D1`, `sonnet 1m` on a todo row with a running linked agent), the gate's state glyph in the SIGNALS glyph cell, and the signals' value-left, meta-right split.
implementationNotes:
- New `hooks/companion.ts` (Client surface module): the frame table above, `moodOf(props)` ('rest' | 'ask' | 'red' | 'done'), local state {mood, lastGateAt, blinkAt, phase, drawn}, one `every(250)` started on the first call, a hop when a passed gate in props is newer than `lastGateAt`, setState only when the due frame differs from `drawn`; body and eyes in `claude` (eyes `inverseText` on a `claude` background), the `companion` setting choosing full/face/off.
- `drawPane`'s header becomes the nook: `<Box flexDirection="row" gap={1}>` holding the 4x3 Client (or a `◉` Text in `claude` where there is no Client) and a `flexGrow` column of the three nameplate rows (health · title · flexGrow · elapsed; branch · gate command · flexGrow · `n agents`; meter · count). Nothing else in the pane is indented.
- `bandSegments`: at `columns >= 100` prepend `{ key: 'face', text: '◉ ', tone: 'claude', drop: 0 }` to `left`, so the face is inside the width budget and the title clip absorbs it; `drawBand` draws it through the existing Text branch. The count/step join stays as today. Test: at 100 columns with a 55-character step title, `width(left) + width(right) + 5 <= 100`; at 60 columns the face is absent and the kept segments are health, count, step, gate.
- Replace `rule()` with `sectionHead(key, label, right?)`: `marginTop={1}`, dim bold label at the left edge, `flexGrow` spacer, optional right-edge summary (phase chips for PLAN; nothing for NEEDS YOU and SIGNALS); delete `ruleParts` and the `isMono` branch for section heads.
- One row shape, `edgeRow(glyph?, text, fact?)`: a one-cell glyph Text (an empty one-cell Text when there is no state), one space, the text (clipped with `…` two cells short of the fact), a `flexGrow` spacer, the fact in dim (or its own tone). `stepRow` drops its level indents and uses it; the phase row is an `edgeRow` with `▶` bold and the count as the fact; new facts: `? D1` in warning when a decision's `blocks === step.id`, and `shortModel + ago` on a todo row when a running agent is linked to it. `needsBlock` uses it with `blocks B4` / the drift age as the fact. Keyed rows and option buttons get `hover: { backgroundColor: bg2 }` with bg2 the slate pair chosen from the `theme` row of `$.config.list()` (light* -> light value, else dark), read at session start and on `config.set` events with key `theme`, and passed in the view data.
- `signalsBlock`: three `edgeRow`s: gate (glyph `✓`/`●`/`✗` in its tone, text dim `gate` + `passed 4m ago`, fact `took 52s`), git (no glyph, `git 9e1d0aa 2m ago`, fact `6 today`), ctx (no glyph, `ctx 61%`, fact `$4.10`). `logBlock`: `edgeRow` with the entry kind as glyph and the time as fact. `stepDetail`'s `field`: dim name and value as the text, sha/time as the fact. Drop every `padEnd` and every fixed label width.
- Footer: plain Buttons with bare-name labels, the active tab's label a bold Text chip, the Needs-you count a warning chip, `gap={3}`; the hotkey chrome is the engine's.
- Tests: `bandSegments` at 60 and 100 with and without the face; `moodOf` transitions; the hop trigger on a newer passed gate; the bg2 pick returning the slate pair from a theme string; a render of the 72-column overview against the sample data asserting that every row below the nook starts its glyph or label at cell 2 (text at cell 4) and every right-edge fact ends on cell 71, plus a snapshot.
